title: Projection ladder has a finite optimal granularity
hypothesis: A large semantic projection gap can create recognition friction; inserting intermediate representations can reduce jump friction, but too many representations add overhead.

model.homogeneous_cost: J(n) = alpha * D^2 / n + beta * n

theorem_boundary: For D>0, alpha>0, beta>0, J is strictly convex over positive real n and has a unique finite continuous minimum at n*.
adaptive_extension: For local span j with difficulty w_j and distance d_j, n_j* = d_j * sqrt(alpha*w_j/beta); harder semantic transitions receive finer subdivision.
invariants: One giant projection can be unnecessarily expensive
Infinite explanatory granularity is not optimal
Optimal granularity depends on user/task friction and stage overhead
High-difficulty edges deserve denser intermediate representations
boundary: This is a design theorem for a declared friction surrogate. It is not a quantitative model of human working memory or neural processing.
